methodology.ac5RegenerabilityStatus: partial, and narrower than before — AC5 as literally worded ('is regenerable by re-running the phase-1 CLI') is still not fully met: runSet and the whole-corpus agentContextFloor (legacyRegression/correctedRegression/measuredFloor/attribution) do not regenerate from the shipped CLI (see regenerateCommandScope). The add-per-agent-class-floor phase closed one slice of this gap — floorByAgentClass now regenerates exactly via the CLI's --format json, sourced from the same regenerateCommand — without re-baselining or otherwise touching runSet/byAgentClass/agentContextFloor/totalsDiscrepancy/warnings, which remain exactly as this phase (2) left them. Closing the remainder in full still requires adding output modes to scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs for runSet enumeration and the whole-corpus regression figures, which this phase's own AC7 ("no reduction change is made in this phase") forbids touching. AC7 is kept satisfied; the remainder of AC5 is tracked as follow-up task measure-lane-tokens-regenerability-gap.

floorByAgentClass.description: Per-agent-class first-request floor: median (n/min/p10/mean) of each measured agent's first transcript request only (uncachedInput + cacheWrite + cacheRead, before any tool use) -- the same definition agentContextFloor.measuredFloor uses, broken out per agentClass instead of a single whole-corpus figure.
floorByAgentClass.source: this phase's own regenerateCommand (see methodology.regenerateCommand), re-run against the existing on-disk corpus -- no fresh dispatch; every record counted predates this phase's own code change
floorByAgentClass.zeroValueNote: 6 records in this regeneration have firstRequestTokens === 0 (contributing the minTokens: 0 seen on estimate/plan/refute below) -- the same count as, and consistent with, agentContextFloor's already-documented 'excluding 6 agents with a tokens value of exactly 0 - orphaned zero-usage transcript entries, not real observations'. This addendum does NOT apply that exclusion -- it counts every record with a non-null firstRequestTokens, including zero-valued ones -- because the approved scope of this phase excludes only cached/sidecarOnly (null) records, not zero-valued measured ones; a future phase revisiting this exclusion should treat it as a methodology decision, not a bug.
floorByAgentClass.populationCaveat: The corpus grew between phase 2's measurement (runSet.included: 40 runs / 1943 records) and this regeneration (44 runs / 2110 records) -- this is corpus growth between measurements, not a re-baseline; runSet/byAgentClass/agentContextFloor above remain byte-unchanged from phase 2. Summing n across every class below gives 2086, a 24-record gap against this regeneration's own recordCount of 2110 -- consistent with the 23-record gap phase 2 already noted between agentContextFloor.measuredFloor.n (1920) and runSet.included.totalAgentRecords (1943); in both cases the gap is exactly the count of cached/sidecarOnly records excluded from the floor population, not an error.

mixedBucketCaveat.estimate: Mixes mechanical (estimate:list/write:*/tier:*) and judgment (estimate:rate:*) sub-labels under one agentClass bucket, because agentClassFromLabel groups purely on the string before the first colon -- this figure must NOT be read as a clean mechanical-only floor.
mixedBucketCaveat.act: Mixes mechanical (act:round-note:*, irreducible per docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md) and judgment (act:code, act:<kind>:<ident>) sub-labels under the same one-bucket-per-colon-split rule -- this figure must NOT be read as a clean mechanical-only floor either, mirroring the estimate caveat above.

mechanicalContextTrim.description: Comparison point for the mechanical-agent context trim (agentType / effort), plus the measured size of the trim itself. preChangeMedianTokens below PINS the pre-change side of the eventual lane comparison so a later run cannot silently re-baseline it. No post-change LANE corpus exists (no agent() call site was edited), but the per-agent effect of agentType and of CLAUDE.md was measured directly -- see measuredTrim2x2.
mechanicalContextTrim.status: trim-measured-directly; agentType UNUSABLE from the Workflow runtime; no post-change lane corpus
mechanicalContextTrim.statusReason: The phase is feasibility-gated on a spike (.claude/workflows/spike-agent-type.js). It HAS NOW BEEN RUN via the Workflow tool -- run wf_2bea58b9-38f (8 cases, 5 OK / 3 threw) plus follow-up probe wf_6cca94eb-de0 -- and its result is recorded under workflowPathSpike below. Two answers changed. (1) agentType does NOT resolve from inside a Workflow run: agent({agentType:'rdm-mechanical'}) RAISED `agent type not found`, and the registry it reported held only built-in agent types, no project-local definition at all. That makes the 19894-token trim measured but currently undeliverable at any call site, local-only workflows included -- not merely blocked downstream. (2) effort:'low' passed to agent() IS honored (see effortDecision), reversing the definition-side negative. The context-floor figures in measuredTrim2x2 are unaffected: they come from a controlled 2x2 over `claude -p` sessions, which resolve the .claude/agents/ registry successfully and record the SAME per-request usage that scripts/lib/token-report.mjs reads. No agent() call site was edited, so there is still no post-change LANE corpus and no floorByAgentClass delta to report. See docs/workflow-schemas.md § 'agentType / effort options spike' for the full evidence tables and the disposition.

workflowPathSpike.description: The live Workflow-tool dispatch of .claude/workflows/spike-agent-type.js. This is the call path the actual call sites use, so where it disagrees with the `claude -p` measurement it governs.
workflowPathSpike.agentTypeEvidence: Cases B ('rdm-mechanical'), C ('no-such-agent-xyz') and F ('rdm-mechanical' + effort) all THREW the identical error: `agent({agentType}): agent type '<X>' not found. Available agents: claude, claude-code-guide, Explore, general-purpose, Plan, statusline-setup`. That list contains only built-in/plugin agent types -- no project-local definition. The definition file was copied into the DISPATCHING SESSION's project root before the run (a Workflow run resolves the session's registry, not the script's directory) and was still not found; probe wf_6cca94eb-de0 re-ran the same case minutes later and threw identically, so the registry is a session-start snapshot that does not refresh.
workflowPathSpike.agentTypeFailureModeNote: Previously INFERRED from a runtime string table; now observed 4x. The spike script distinguishes a throw from a null return explicitly, so the shape is unambiguous. Contrast an unknown `model` id, which resolves agent() to null silently.
workflowPathSpike.unresolvedHypotheses: Cannot separate H1 (a Workflow run never consults a project-local .claude/agents/) from H2 (it does, but only as snapshotted at session start). Both carry the SAME operational consequence: an agentType literal in a workflow script raises on first dispatch from any session whose start-of-session registry lacks the definition -- which includes every session rooted outside this worktree. No separation was needed in order to decide not to thread.
workflowPathSpike.scopeConsequence: This removes the local-only-vs-distributed distinction the phase plan relied on. verify-workflow-review.sh §2b greps only rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js, so threading the four local-only workflows would have passed every gate in the repo and still broken them on first dispatch.
workflowPathSpike.firstRequestTokensNote: Identical across all 5 OK cases, which is expected: every one ran as the DEFAULT agent because no agentType ever resolved. The run therefore yields NO Workflow-path floor measurement, and measuredTrim2x2 remains the only floor evidence. Not comparable to the 2x2 cells -- different prompt, different session.
workflowPathSpike.structuredReturnNote: The follow-up task's scope item 3 (does agent(prompt,{schema}) still work under `tools: Bash, StructuredOutput`, and is agentType honored through parallel()) could NOT be exercised, because nothing resolved.

measuredTrim2x2.description: Controlled 2x2, run live in this worktree on claude-opus-5, one identical trivial prompt per cell. Factor A: session default agent vs `claude --agent rdm-mechanical` (this repo's .claude/agents/ definition). Factor B: project CLAUDE.md present vs temporarily moved aside and restored. The user-global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is present in all four cells and cancels out of every difference.
measuredTrim2x2.metric: firstRequestTokens = input + cache_creation + cache_read on the session's first assistant record -- the same quantity buildRecords computes per agent, so it is directly comparable to floorByAgentClass. Cache-placement-independent by construction.

agentTypeTrimTokens.note: The two margins agree to within 11 tokens (0.06%), so the agentType effect and the CLAUDE.md effect are independent and additive. This is the whole prize on offer: the default agent's system prompt plus the tool schemas of every tool rdm-mechanical does not receive.

claudeMdCostTokens.note: Equal to within 11 tokens: a custom agentType pays the FULL project-memory cost. A trimmed system prompt and a two-tool allowlist displace none of it.

claudeMdFinding.implicationForAttribution: agentContextFloor.attribution uses chars/4 and is left UNCHANGED as the recorded phase-2 figure, but it is now known to understate this file by 60%. At the measured 2.49 chars/token, claudeMdSubtotal's 61247 chars price at roughly 24600 tokens rather than 15312, and remainderToolSchemasSystemPrompt (23526) is overstated by the same amount since it is derived as floor minus that subtotal.
claudeMdFinding.avoidabilityEvidence: The runtime's agent-definition frontmatter schema accepts description, tools, disallowedTools, prompt, model, effort, permissionMode, mcpServers, hooks, maxTurns, color, background, memory, isolation, observer, observerMessage, observeSubagents -- none suppresses CLAUDE.md. `memory` is E.enum(["user","project","local"]) scoping auto-loading of ~/.claude/agent-memory/ files, i.e. it ADDS context. The only suppression switches are process-global: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS, and --bare / CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 (which also strips hooks, LSP and auth).
claudeMdFinding.disposition: Per the phase body: recorded as a finding, and not pursued further. No CLAUDE.md restructuring was attempted or is proposed. The measurement only reprices the option -- a hypothetical 30% CLAUDE.md reduction would be worth ~5800 tokens per agent, not the ~3600 the chars/4 estimate implied.

corroborationCrossProject.description: Independent corroboration from the existing on-disk corpus: per-agent-class median firstRequestTokens grouped by project slug, for two repos whose CLAUDE.md files differ by 31144 chars (rdm 48207, bowling-app 17063) and which share the same user-global copy.
corroborationCrossProject.caveat: CORROBORATING ONLY. The two repos differ in skills, hooks and prompt sizes as well as CLAUDE.md, so this cannot isolate CLAUDE.md the way measuredTrim2x2 does. It is reported because it reproduces the same 'chars/4 understates by roughly half again' signature from an entirely different dataset.

mechanicalContextTrim.mustNotCompareAgainst: agentContextFloor.measuredFloor.reportedFloorTokens (38837.5) and agentContextFloor.legacyRegression.interceptTokens (37552) -- both are WHOLE-CORPUS figures, not per-class ones; comparing a mechanical-class median against either measures corpus composition, not the change.
mechanicalContextTrim.measurementProtocolForTheFollowUp: Scope the fresh run with --since <ISO date of the first post-change run> so the pre-change corpus is not averaged in: `node scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs --format json --since <date> --workflow autopilot --workflow dispatch-phase --workflow plan-review --workflow backlog --workflow estimate --workflow document`, then read report.floorByAgentClass. A single fresh dispatch yields single-digit n per class, so the resulting delta is DIRECTIONAL, not a re-baseline -- record n per class alongside it and do not overwrite the figures above.
mechanicalContextTrim.effortDecision: NOT applied at any call site -- but as of the Workflow-path run the reason is SCOPE, not inertness. The two routes were measured separately and they DISAGREE. Route 1, definition-side (effort:"low" in the agent frontmatter, via --agents, whose zod schema carries effort: E.union([E.enum(vO), E.number().int()]).optional()): the agent resolved, ran normally, and its first assistant record still said effort:"high" -- accepted, not honored. Route 2, call-site (agent(prompt, {effort:'low'}) from inside a Workflow run, spike case E): the transcript recorded effort:"low" -- HONORED. Against the fixed control (across 6290 transcripts / 156384 assistant records the top-level `effort` field holds only "high" (55945) or is absent (100439), and "low" ZERO times) a single "low" record is conclusive, and case E is that record; the four sibling cases in the same run all recorded "high". Case H additionally shows an INVALID effort value is accepted and silently degrades to "high" rather than throwing -- the opposite of agentType, where a bad value takes the lane down. scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh §2b still fails if any workflow script passes effort:, now because the phase body forbids threading it (step 4, written on the strength of the definition-side negative that route 2 overturned), not because the option is inert. Flipping that gated invariant across ~15 call sites is a scope decision for the roadmap owner. Carried by task finish-agent-type-effort-spike-and-thread-mechanical-sites scope item 5, which is now live and unblocked. Limits on the positive: n=1 per cell, and the run measured only that the request RAN at low -- not whether low effort degrades mechanical transcription fidelity, which the follow-up must establish before shipping it.

confounds: roadmap size - a roadmap with more phases dispatches more dispatch-phase/plan-review/estimate agent invocations inside a single autopilot run; larger roadmap does not imply a more expensive phase
phase difficulty / model tier - rdm-estimate assigns each phase a difficulty and model tier; a high-tier phase's agents run on a more expensive model and do not necessarily use fewer tokens for it

rework rounds - a phase that bounces through plan-review or code-review rework re-runs find/refute/plan/implement agents multiple times; its total is not comparable to a phase that passed on the first pass

user-specific CLAUDE.md - the user-global CLAUDE.md measured for the context floor is this operator's own machine; a different operator's global instructions file will shift the floor by a different amount

model-identity drift - some agent records carry a generic alias (haiku, sonnet) rather than a resolved snapshot ID and contribute zero measurable usage; per-model comparisons must key on the exact snapshot ID
run completeness - 3 of 19 autopilot runs in scope are killed and 4 are failed (0 agents)
comparableUnit: per-agent-class figures and per-phase-dispatch figures; raw per-run totals are not a valid comparison unit for later phases' before/after claims

noBehaviorChange.statement: measurement and documentation only; no file under .claude/workflows/, .claude/workflows/lib/, .claude/skills/, scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs, or scripts/lib/token-report.mjs was modified by this phase's commit
